## Current en content:
# Frequently asked questions

### How do I become a member?

Fill in the form on the membership page.

### Do I need to know how to swim?

Yes, all members must be able to swim 200 metres.

### Is there an age limit?

Juniors can start rowing from the age of 12.

### When does the season start?

The season starts in April, when the ice has gone.

### Can I try before joining?

Yes, we hold try-out evenings every Tuesday in May.

### What should I wear?

Tight-fitting sports clothes that you can move in.

### Do I get a key to the boathouse?

Yes, the key deposit is 100 SEK.

### Can I bring a guest?

Guests may row twice per season with a member.

### Is coaching included?

Coaching on Tuesdays and Thursdays is included in the fee.

### Can I row alone?

Only after passing the sculling test.

### What happens in bad weather?

The duty officer decides whether boats may go out.

### Do you race?

We enter three regattas each summer.

### Is there a gym?

Yes, the gym is open all year round.

### Can I rent a boat?

Boats are for members only and cannot be rented.

### How do I book a boat?

Book in the app at least one hour ahead.

### Are there showers?

Yes, there are showers and a sauna in the clubhouse.

### Can I store my own boat?

Private boats can be stored for a fee if there is room.

### Do you have lockers?

Yes, lockers cost 150 SEK per season.

### Is there parking?

Parking is free behind the boathouse.

### Do you organise social events?

Yes, we hold a spring party and an autumn dinner.

### How do I cancel my membership?

Email the treasurer before 1 December.

### Can I pause my membership?

You can pause for one season at a time.

### Who runs the club?

A board elected at the annual meeting in March.

### How can I help out?

Sign up for a work day on the club calendar.

# Frequently asked questions

### How do I become a member?

Fill in the form on the membership page.

### Do I need to know how to swim?

Yes, all members must be able to swim 300 metres.

### Is there an age limit?

Juniors can start rowing from the age of 12.

### When does the season start?

The season starts in April, when the ice has gone.

### Can I try before joining?

Yes, we hold try-out evenings every Tuesday in May.

### What should I wear?

Tight-fitting sports clothes that you can move in.

### Do I get a key to the boathouse?

Yes, the key deposit is 100 SEK.

### Can I bring a guest?

Guests may row twice per season with a member.

### Is coaching included?

Coaching on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Sundays is included in the fee.

### Can I row alone?

Only after passing the sculling test.

### What happens in bad weather?

The duty officer decides whether boats may go out.

### Do you race?

We enter three regattas each summer.

### Is there a gym?

Yes, the gym is open all year round.

### Can I rent a boat?

Boats are for members only and cannot be rented.

### How do I book a boat?

Book in the app at least two hours ahead.

### Are there showers?

Yes, there are showers and a sauna in the clubhouse.

### Can I store my own boat?

Private boats can be stored for a fee if there is room.

### Do you have lockers?

Yes, lockers cost 100 SEK per season.

### Is there parking?

Parking is free behind the boathouse.

### Do you organise social events?

Yes, we hold a spring party and an autumn dinner.

### How do I cancel my membership?

Email the treasurer before 1 December.

### Can I pause my membership?

You can pause for one season at a time.

### Who runs the club?

A board elected at the annual meeting in February.

### How can I help out?

Sign up for a work day on the club calendar.

# Frequently asked questions

### How do I become a member?

Fill in the form on the membership page.

### Do I need to know how to swim?

Yes, all members must be able to swim 300 metres.

### Is there an age limit?

Juniors can start rowing from the age of 12.

The season starts in April, when the ice has gone.

### Can I try before joining?

Yes, we hold try-out evenings every Tuesday in May.

### What should I wear?

Tight-fitting sports clothes that you can move in.

### Do I get a key to the boathouse?

Yes, the key deposit is 100 SEK.

### Can I bring a guest?

Guests may row twice per season with a member.

### Is coaching included?

Coaching on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Sundays is included in the fee.

### Can I row alone?

Only after passing the sculling test.

### What happens in bad weather?

The duty officer decides whether boats may go out.

### Do you race?

We enter three regattas each summer.

### Is there a gym?

Yes, the gym is open all year round.

### Can I rent a boat?

Boats are for members only and cannot be rented.

### How do I book a boat?

Book in the app at least two hours ahead.

### Are there showers?

Yes, there are showers and a sauna in the clubhouse.

### Can I store my own boat?

Private boats can be stored for a fee if there is room.

### Do you have lockers?

Yes, lockers cost 100 SEK per season.

### Is there parking?

Parking is free behind the boathouse.

### Do you organise social events?

Yes, we hold a spring party and an autumn dinner.

### How do I cancel my membership?

Email the treasurer before 1 December.

### Can I pause my membership?

You can pause for one season at a time.

### Who runs the club?

A board elected at the annual meeting in February.

Sign up for a work day on the club calendar.

The English page may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose Swedish pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in Swedish follow that convention too. Text a reader sees is Swedish, written as a Swedish writer would put it, not word for word.

prompt.system:
You are keeping the Swedish (sv) translation of a document up to date. Its source is English (en): Swedish was translated from it, and has since been corrected and localized by hand. The English page may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose Swedish pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in Swedish follow that convention too. Text a reader sees is Swedish, written as a Swedish writer would put it, not word for word.

Before you edit, write out briefly: every place where the Swedish page no longer says what the other pages say, quoted from both, with whether you think it is a change waiting to be made in Swedish or a difference on purpose, and why.

Then make the edits, together in one response. Edit with edit_file: its old_string must appear exactly, once, in the Swedish file. Each edit's result shows the Swedish file around it as it now reads. Look at it: if anything there is wrong, was missed, or now contradicts something elsewhere in the Swedish file, fix it with further edits. When the Swedish file is right, say in a sentence or two what you changed and why. If nothing needs to change, make no edit at all, and say why not. Write your plan, your notes and your summary in English, whatever language the documents are in.

# Vanliga frågor

### Hur blir jag medlem?

Fyll i formuläret på medlemssidan.

### Behöver jag kunna simma?

Ja, alla medlemmar måste kunna simma 200 meter.

### Finns det en åldersgräns?

Juniorer kan börja ro från 12 års ålder.

### När börjar säsongen?

Säsongen börjar i april, när isen har gått.

### Kan jag prova innan jag går med?

Ja, vi har prova-på-kvällar varje tisdag i maj.

### Vad ska jag ha på mig?

Åtsittande träningskläder som du kan röra dig i.

### Får jag en nyckel till båthuset?

Ja, depositionen för nyckeln är 100 kr.

### Får jag ta med en gäst?

Gäster får ro två gånger per säsong tillsammans med en medlem.

### Ingår träning med tränare?

Träning med tränare på tisdagar och torsdagar ingår i avgiften.

### Får jag ro ensam?

Först när du har klarat singelprovet.

### Vad händer vid dåligt väder?

Dagens ansvarige bestämmer om båtarna får gå ut.

### Tävlar ni?

Vi deltar i tre regattor varje sommar.

### Finns det ett gym?

Ja, gymmet är öppet året runt.

### Kan jag hyra en båt?

Båtarna är bara för medlemmar och kan inte hyras.

### Hur bokar jag en båt?

Boka i appen minst en timme i förväg.

### Finns det duschar?

Ja, det finns duschar och bastu i klubbhuset.

### Kan jag förvara min egen båt?

Privata båtar kan förvaras mot en avgift om det finns plats.

### Finns det skåp?

Ja, ett skåp kostar 100 kr per säsong.

### Finns det parkering?

Parkeringen bakom båthuset är gratis.

### Ordnar ni sociala aktiviteter?

Ja, vi har en vårfest och en höstmiddag.

### Hur säger jag upp mitt medlemskap?

Mejla kassören före den 1 december.

### Kan jag pausa mitt medlemskap?

Du kan pausa en säsong i taget.

### Vem driver klubben?

En styrelse som väljs på årsmötet i mars.

### Hur kan jag hjälpa till?

Anmäl dig till en arbetsdag i klubbkalendern.

Juniorer kan börja ro från 12 års ålder.

Åtsittande träningskläder som du kan röra dig i.

Gäster får ro två gånger per säsong tillsammans med en medlem.

Dagens ansvarige bestämmer om båtarna får gå ut.

Boka i appen minst en timme i förväg.

Ja, det finns duschar och bastu i klubbhuset.

Privata båtar kan förvaras mot en avgift om det finns plats.

Mejla kassören före den 1 december.

Du kan pausa en säsong i taget.

En styrelse som väljs på årsmötet i mars.

Anmäl dig till en arbetsdag i klubbkalendern.

# Vanliga frågor

### Hur blir jag medlem?

Fyll i formuläret på medlemssidan.

### Behöver jag kunna simma?

Ja, alla medlemmar måste kunna simma 200 meter.

### Finns det en åldersgräns?

Juniorer kan börja ro från 12 års ålder.

### När börjar säsongen?

Säsongen börjar i april, när isen har gått.

### Kan jag prova innan jag går med?

Ja, vi har prova-på-kvällar varje tisdag i maj.

### Vad ska jag ha på mig?

Åtsittande träningskläder som du kan röra dig i.

### Får jag en nyckel till båthuset?

Ja, depositionen för nyckeln är 100 kr.

### Får jag ta med en gäst?

Gäster får ro två gånger per säsong tillsammans med en medlem.

### Ingår träning med tränare?

Träning med tränare på tisdagar och torsdagar ingår i avgiften.

### Får jag ro ensam?

Först när du har klarat singelprovet.

### Vad händer vid dåligt väder?

Dagens ansvarige bestämmer om båtarna får gå ut.

### Tävlar ni?

Vi deltar i tre regattor varje sommar.

### Finns det ett gym?

Ja, gymmet är öppet året runt.

### Kan jag hyra en båt?

Båtarna är bara för medlemmar och kan inte hyras.

### Hur bokar jag en båt?

Boka i appen minst en timme i förväg.

### Finns det duschar?

Ja, det finns duschar och bastu i klubbhuset.

### Kan jag förvara min egen båt?

Privata båtar kan förvaras mot en avgift om det finns plats.

### Finns det skåp?

Ja, ett skåp kostar 100 kr per säsong.

### Finns det parkering?

Parkeringen bakom båthuset är gratis.

### Ordnar ni sociala aktiviteter?

Ja, vi har en vårfest och en höstmiddag.

### Hur säger jag upp mitt medlemskap?

Mejla kassören före den 1 december.

### Kan jag pausa mitt medlemskap?

Du kan pausa en säsong i taget.

### Vem driver klubben?

En styrelse som väljs på årsmötet i mars.

### Hur kan jag hjälpa till?

Anmäl dig till en arbetsdag i klubbkalendern.

You are keeping the Swedish (sv) translation of a document up to date. Its source is English (en): Swedish was translated from it, and has since been corrected and localized by hand. The English page may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose Swedish pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in Swedish follow that convention too. Text a reader sees is Swedish, written as a Swedish writer would put it, not word for word.

Before you edit, write out briefly: every place where the Swedish page no longer says what the other pages say, quoted from both, with whether you think it is a change waiting to be made in Swedish or a difference on purpose, and why.

Then make the edits, together in one response. Edit with edit_file: its old_string must appear exactly, once, in the Swedish file. Each edit's result shows the Swedish file around it as it now reads. Look at it: if anything there is wrong, was missed, or now contradicts something elsewhere in the Swedish file, fix it with further edits. When the Swedish file is right, say in a sentence or two what you changed and why. If nothing needs to change, make no edit at all, and say why not. - A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. import { CmBandHeading } from '@acme/blocks/CmBandHeading';
import { CmButton } from '@acme/blocks/CmButton';
import { CmColumn, CmColumns } from '@acme/blocks/CmColumns';

import { CmSection } from '@acme/blocks/CmSection';
import { TextBlock } from '@acme/blocks/TextBlock';

<CmHero id="hero-a1b2c3d4"
  title="Acme"
  subtitle="Acme är världens bästa turneringssystem för världens bästa turneringar"
  ctaText="Läs mer om Acme"
  ctaLink="/sv/missa-inte/"
  backgroundMedia="/media/start-video-002-optimized.mp4"
  poster="/media/home/hero-poster.jpg"
/>

<CmSection id="sect-e5f6a7b8"
  heading="Vad är Acme?"
  contain="true"
  align="left"
  body={"Acme hjälper dig som arrangerar turneringar att enkelt och smidigt ge en fantastisk helhetsupplevelse till dina deltagare. Från anmälning, betallösning, lottning och spelschema till liverapportering av mål och slutresultat till webb, mobilappar eller sms.\n\nVi har gjort det enkelt för stora, små, enkla och komplexa turneringar."}
  divider={true}
  contained={true}
/>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-4a6e82d1"
  eyebrow="ENKLA BETALLÖSNINGAR"
  title="Ta enkelt betalt med kort, Klarna eller Swish"
  ctaText="Läs mer om vår betallösning"
  ctaLink="/sv/kort-och-klarna/"
  image="/media/home/klarna_acme-3.webp"
  imageAlt="Betalning med Klarna i Acme"
  imagePosition="right"
  bgColor="light"
  imageFocus="left center"
>
  Med vår moderna betallösning kan ni slippa alla bankbetalningar. Låt lagen betala med kort eller Klarna vilket gör att betalningarna registreras automatiskt i systemet och ni får era pengar direkt.
</CmFeatureRow>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-2c8d91e4"
  eyebrow="Smartare schemaläggning med AI"
  title="Så fungerar det i Acme"
  ctaText="Läs mer om AI i Acme här"
  ctaLink="/sv/vara-ai-losningar/"
  image="/media/home/ai-image-copy-1.webp"
  imageAlt="AI-schemaläggning i Acme"
  imagePosition="left"
  bgColor="white"
>
  Att lägga ett fungerande spelschema är ett komplext pussel – särskilt när det handlar om hundratals eller tusentals matcher, flera spelplatser, vilotider och specialönskemål.
</CmFeatureRow>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-91d5c0e7"
  eyebrow="VI ÄR STOLTA ÖVER VÅR SUPPORT"
  title="Support i världsklass"
  ctaText="Läs mer om vår support här"
  ctaLink="/sv/support/"
  image="/media/home/support.webp"
  imageAlt="Acme-supporten"
  imagePosition="left"
  bgColor="white"
>
  Den kanske mest definierande delen av Acme är vår support. Vi arbetar hårt för att alla i företaget har som yttersta mål att hjälpa våra kunder. Vi finns tillgängliga varje dag för att hjälpa er med allt från enskilda frågor till att assistera med spelschema och rådgivning.
</CmFeatureRow>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-5b0e7a13"
  eyebrow="LIVESTREAMING MED GLOBEX LIVE"
  title="Sänd alla matcher live – och tjäna pengar på det"
  ctaText="Läs mer om livestreaming"
  ctaLink="/sv/streaming/"
  image="/media/streaming/pix4team-camera.gif"
  imageAlt="AI-kamera på stativ som automatiskt följer matchen"
  imagePosition="right"
  bgColor="light"
>
  Tillsammans med vår partner Globex Live kan ni livestreama alla matcher med AI-kameror som följer spelet automatiskt. Tittarna betalar per match eller för hela turneringen – en ny intäktskälla för cupen.
</CmFeatureRow>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-c3b90f52"
  eyebrow="ENGAGERA ERA BESÖKARE"
  title="Er egen mobilapp för Android och iPhone"
  ctaText="Skaffa en app för er turnering"
  ctaLink="/sv/app/"
  image="/media/home/usp-mobile-app.jpg"
  imageAlt="Egen mobilapp för turneringen"
  imagePosition="left"
  bgColor="white"
>
  Vi kan hjälpa er att få er egen mobilapp för turneringen. Vi gör allt arbete med att utveckla appen och den blir sedan kopplad till turneringen i Acme vilket gör att ni kan administrera allt från ett och samma ställe.
</CmFeatureRow>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-7f04b3a9"
  eyebrow="CASE STUDIE: FJORDBY BASKET FESTIVAL"
  title="En av våra kunder berättar"
  ctaText="Läs om Fjordby Basket Festival här"
  ctaLink="/sv/fjordby-basket-festival/"
  image="/media/home/customer-story.png"
  imageAlt="Fjordby Basket Festival"
  imagePosition="right"
  bgColor="light"
>
  Läs vårt reportage om en lyckad resa för basket och Fjordby i Norge. Ola Nordvik berättar lite om deras resa, hur de avancerat, lyckats och fortsätter att sätta upp nya mål i framtiden med sin turnering.
</CmFeatureRow>

<CmBandHeading id="band-5e17d8f0"
  heading="Mer information för den intresserade"
  bg="white"
  align="left"
  contained={true}
/>

<CmColumns id="cols-8b2f47c6"
  align="left"
  columns="2"
  gap="48"
  maxWidth={1140}
>
  <CmColumn id="col-d94a10e3"
    heading="Viktiga funktioner"
  >
    <TextBlock id="text-6c58e2b7">
      Missa inte att vi också har häftiga funktioner som livestreaming med Globex Live, liveresultat, egen hemsida för turneringen, boende & mat, domare, SMS-utskick och incheckning.
    </TextBlock>
    <CmButton id="btn-31f7a9d0"
      label="Läs mer om våra funktioner"
      href="/sv/missa-inte/"
      variant="green"
      icon="none"
    />
  </CmColumn>
  <CmColumn id="col-59a3e8d7"
    heading="Prissättning"
  >
    <TextBlock id="text-c21f80b4">
      Vi har en enkel prissättning som passar både små och stora turneringar i olika sporter. Förutom en lagbaserad licens finns det många extratjänster att välja till!
    </TextBlock>
    <CmButton id="btn-e40b97c3"
      label="Läs mer om våra priser"
      href="/sv/priser/"
      variant="green"
      icon="none"
    />
  </CmColumn>
</CmColumns>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-06c9e3b8"
  eyebrow="TA BETALT FÖR FÖRENINGEN"
  title="Acme Clubs"
  ctaText="Läs mer om Acme Clubs"
  ctaLink="https://clubs.acme.example/"
  image="/media/home/si.jpg"
  imageAlt="Acme Clubs"
  imagePosition="right"
  bgColor="light"
>
  Vår systerprodukt Acme Clubs används av uppemot 1000 klubbar för att samla in träningsavgifter och medlemsavgifter, i både Norge och Sverige. Systemet låter dig anpassa er insamling samtidigt som det är väldigt lättanvänt.
</CmFeatureRow>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-f15b72a0"
  eyebrow="IDROTT ÄR VIKTIGT I EN GLOBAL VÄRLD"
  title="Gemenskap, hopp och utveckling – både här hemma och i Östafrika."
  ctaText="Läs mer om samarbetet"
  ctaLink="/sv/lakeside-youth-cup/"
  image="/media/home/LakesideYouthCup.webp"
  imageAlt="Lakeside Youth Cup"
  imagePosition="left"
  bgColor="light"
>
  Vi samarbetar med Lakeside Youth Cup (LYC), en årlig ungdomsfestival i Tanzania som stärker unga genom idrott, utbildning och samhällsengagemang.
</CmFeatureRow>

The English page may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose Swedish pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in Swedish follow that convention too. Text a reader sees is Swedish, written as a Swedish writer would put it, not word for word.

Before you edit, write out briefly: every place where the Swedish page no longer says what the other pages say, quoted from both, with whether you think it is a change waiting to be made in Swedish or a difference on purpose, and why.

Then make the edits, together in one response. Edit with edit_file: its old_string must appear exactly, once, in the Swedish file. Each edit's result shows the Swedish file around it as it now reads. Look at it: if anything there is wrong, was missed, or now contradicts something elsewhere in the Swedish file, fix it with further edits. When the Swedish file is right, say in a sentence or two what you changed and why. If nothing needs to change, make no edit at all, and say why not. Write your plan, your notes and your summary in English, whatever language the documents are in.

prompt.system:
You are keeping the Swedish (sv) translation of a document up to date. Its source is English (en): Swedish was translated from it, and has since been corrected and localized by hand. The English page may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose Swedish pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in Swedish follow that convention too. Text a reader sees is Swedish, written as a Swedish writer would put it, not word for word.

Before you edit, write out briefly: every place where the Swedish page no longer says what the other pages say, quoted from both, with whether you think it is a change waiting to be made in Swedish or a difference on purpose, and why.

Then make the edits, together in one response. Edit with edit_file: its old_string must appear exactly, once, in the Swedish file. Each edit's result shows the Swedish file around it as it now reads. Look at it: if anything there is wrong, was missed, or now contradicts something elsewhere in the Swedish file, fix it with further edits. When the Swedish file is right, say in a sentence or two what you changed and why. If nothing needs to change, make no edit at all, and say why not. Write your plan, your notes and your summary in English, whatever language the documents are in.

The English page may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose Swedish pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in Swedish follow that convention too. Text a reader sees is Swedish, written as a Swedish writer would put it, not word for word.

  ctaText="Learn more about Acme"

  backgroundMedia="/media/start-video-002-optimized.mp4"
  poster="/media/home/hero-poster.jpg"
/>

<CmSection id="sect-e5f6a7b8"
  heading="What is Acme?"
  contain="true"
  align="left"
  body={"Acme helps you as a tournament organiser deliver a smooth, fantastic overall experience to your participants. From registration, payment, draws and match schedules to live reporting of goals and final results on the web, in mobile apps or via SMS.\n\nWe've made it simple for tournaments of every size and complexity, big or small."}
  divider={true}
  contained={true}
/>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-2c8d91e4"
  eyebrow="Smarter scheduling with AI"
  title="How it works in Acme"
  ctaText="Read more about AI in Acme here"
  ctaLink="/en/vara-ai-losningar/"
  image="/media/home/ai-image-copy-1.webp"
  imageAlt="AI scheduling in Acme"
  imagePosition="left"
  bgColor="white"
>
  Building a match schedule that actually works is a complex puzzle – especially with hundreds or thousands of matches, multiple venues, rest periods and special requests to consider.
</CmFeatureRow>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-7f04b3a9"
  eyebrow="CASE STUDY: FJORDBY BASKET FESTIVAL"
  title="One of our customers shares their story"
  ctaText="Read about Fjordby Basket Festival here"
  ctaLink="/en/fjordby-basket-festival/"
  image="/media/home/customer-story.png"
  imageAlt="Fjordby Basket Festival"
  imagePosition="right"
  bgColor="light"
>
  Read our feature on a successful journey for basketball and Fjordby, Norway. Ola Nordvik talks about their journey – how they've grown, what they've achieved, and the new goals they keep setting for their tournament's future.
</CmFeatureRow>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-91d5c0e7"
  eyebrow="WE'RE PROUD OF OUR SUPPORT"
  title="World-class support"
  ctaText="Read more about our support here"
  ctaLink="/en/support/"
  image="/media/home/support.webp"
  imageAlt="The Acme support team"
  imagePosition="left"
  bgColor="white"
>

</CmFeatureRow>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-4a6e82d1"
  eyebrow="SIMPLE PAYMENT SOLUTIONS"
  title="Accept card, Klarna or Swish payments with ease"
  ctaText="Read more about our payment solution"
  ctaLink="/en/kort-och-klarna/"
  image="/media/home/klarna_acme-3.webp"
  imageAlt="Payment with Klarna in Acme"
  imagePosition="right"
  bgColor="light"
  imageFocus="left center"
>
  Our modern payment solution means you can skip bank transfers entirely. Let teams pay by card or Klarna, so payments are registered automatically in the system and the money lands in your account right away.
</CmFeatureRow>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-c3b90f52"
  eyebrow="ENGAGE YOUR VISITORS"
  title="Your own mobile app for Android and iPhone"
  ctaText="Get an app for your tournament"
  ctaLink="/en/app/"
  image="/media/home/usp-mobile-app.jpg"
  imageAlt="A dedicated mobile app for the tournament"
  imagePosition="left"
  bgColor="white"

</CmFeatureRow>

  heading="More information for the interested"
  bg="white"
  align="left"
  contained={true}

  columns="2"

    </TextBlock>
    <CmButton id="btn-31f7a9d0"
      label="Read more about our features"
      href="/en/missa-inte/"
      variant="green"
      icon="none"

  <CmColumn id="col-59a3e8d7"
    heading="Pricing"
  >
    <TextBlock id="text-c21f80b4">

    </TextBlock>
    <CmButton id="btn-e40b97c3"
      label="Read more about our pricing"
      href="/en/priser/"
      variant="green"
      icon="none"
    />
  </CmColumn>
</CmColumns>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-06c9e3b8"

  ctaLink="https://clubs.acme.example/"
  image="/media/home/si.jpg"
  imageAlt="Acme Clubs"
  imagePosition="right"
  bgColor="light"
>
  Our sister product Acme Clubs is used by close to 1,000 clubs across Norway and Sweden to collect training fees and membership dues. It lets you tailor your collection to your needs while staying easy to use. Plans start at SEK 95 per month.
</CmFeatureRow>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-f15b72a0"

  title="Community, hope and growth – both at home and in East Africa."
  ctaText="Read more about the partnership"

  image="/media/home/LakesideYouthCup.webp"

  imagePosition="left"
  bgColor="light"

</CmFeatureRow>

The English page may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. The English page may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:

- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. The Swedish page may have changed since English was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current English page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the English page up to date with the current Swedish page: find what it says that English does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the English page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in English: everywhere English states it, so that English does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when English says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder English.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for English. Then do not guess. Markup is not text. The Swedish page may have changed since English was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current English page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the English page up to date with the current Swedish page: find what it says that English does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the English page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in English: everywhere English states it, so that English does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when English says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder English.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for English. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. The Swedish page may have changed since English was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current English page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the English page up to date with the current Swedish page: find what it says that English does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the English page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in English: everywhere English states it, so that English does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when English says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder English.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for English. Then do not guess. You are keeping the Swedish (sv) translation of a document up to date. Its source is English (en): Swedish was translated from it, and has since been corrected and localized by hand. The English page may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose Swedish pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in Swedish follow that convention too. Text a reader sees is Swedish, written as a Swedish writer would put it, not word for word.

Before you edit, write out briefly: every place where the Swedish page no longer says what the other pages say, quoted from both, with whether you think it is a change waiting to be made in Swedish or a difference on purpose, and why.

Look at it: if anything there is wrong, was missed, or now contradicts something elsewhere in the Swedish file, fix it with further edits. When the Swedish file is right, say in a sentence or two what you changed and why. If nothing needs to change, make no edit at all, and say why not. You are keeping the Swedish (sv) translation of a document up to date. Its source is English (en): Swedish was translated from it, and has since been corrected and localized by hand. The English page may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose Swedish pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in Swedish follow that convention too. Text a reader sees is Swedish, written as a Swedish writer would put it, not word for word.

Before you edit, write out briefly: every place where the Swedish page no longer says what the other pages say, quoted from both, with whether you think it is a change waiting to be made in Swedish or a difference on purpose, and why.

Then make the edits, together in one response. Edit with edit_file: its old_string must appear exactly, once, in the Swedish file. Each edit's result shows the Swedish file around it as it now reads. Look at it: if anything there is wrong, was missed, or now contradicts something elsewhere in the Swedish file, fix it with further edits. When the Swedish file is right, say in a sentence or two what you changed and why. If nothing needs to change, make no edit at all, and say why not. Write your plan, your notes and your summary in English, whatever language the documents are in.

import { TextBlock } from '@acme/blocks/TextBlock';

<CmHero id="hero-a1b2c3d4"
  title="Acme"
  subtitle="Acme är världens bästa turneringssystem för världens bästa turneringar"
  ctaText="Läs mer om Acme"
  ctaLink="/sv/missa-inte/"
  backgroundMedia="/media/start-video-002-optimized.mp4"
  poster="/media/home/hero-poster.jpg"
/>

<CmSection id="sect-e5f6a7b8"
  heading="Vad är Acme?"
  contain="true"
  align="left"
  body={"Acme hjälper dig som arrangerar turneringar att enkelt och smidigt ge en fantastisk helhetsupplevelse till dina deltagare. Från anmälning, betallösning, lottning och spelschema till liverapportering av mål och slutresultat till webb, mobilappar eller sms.\n\nVi har gjort det enkelt för stora, små, enkla och komplexa turneringar."}
  divider={true}
  contained={true}
/>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-4a6e82d1"
  eyebrow="ENKLA BETALLÖSNINGAR"
  title="Ta enkelt betalt med kort, Klarna eller Swish"
  ctaText="Läs mer om vår betallösning"
  ctaLink="/sv/kort-och-klarna/"
  image="/media/home/klarna_acme-3.webp"
  imageAlt="Betalning med Klarna i Acme"
  imagePosition="right"
  bgColor="light"
  imageFocus="left center"
>
  Med vår moderna betallösning kan ni slippa alla bankbetalningar. Låt lagen betala med kort eller Klarna vilket gör att betalningarna registreras automatiskt i systemet och ni får era pengar direkt.
</CmFeatureRow>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-2c8d91e4"
  eyebrow="Smartare schemaläggning med AI"
  title="Så fungerar det i Acme"
  ctaText="Läs mer om AI i Acme här"
  ctaLink="/sv/vara-ai-losningar/"
  image="/media/home/ai-image-copy-1.webp"
  imageAlt="AI-schemaläggning i Acme"
  imagePosition="left"
  bgColor="white"
>
  Att lägga ett fungerande spelschema är ett komplext pussel – särskilt när det handlar om hundratals eller tusentals matcher, flera spelplatser, vilotider och specialönskemål.
</CmFeatureRow>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-91d5c0e7"
  eyebrow="VI ÄR STOLTA ÖVER VÅR SUPPORT"
  title="Support i världsklass"
  ctaText="Läs mer om vår support här"
  ctaLink="/sv/support/"
  image="/media/home/support.webp"
  imageAlt="Acme-supporten"
  imagePosition="left"
  bgColor="white"
>
  Den kanske mest definierande delen av Acme är vår support. Vi arbetar hårt för att alla i företaget har som yttersta mål att hjälpa våra kunder. Vi finns tillgängliga varje dag för att hjälpa er med allt från enskilda frågor till att assistera med spelschema och rådgivning. Vi svarar på svenska, norska och engelska.
</CmFeatureRow>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-5b0e7a13"
  eyebrow="LIVESTREAMING MED GLOBEX LIVE"
  title="Sänd alla matcher live – och tjäna pengar på det"
  ctaText="Läs mer om livestreaming"
  ctaLink="/sv/streaming/"
  image="/media/streaming/pix4team-camera.gif"
  imageAlt="AI-kamera på stativ som automatiskt följer matchen"
  imagePosition="right"
  bgColor="light"
>
  Tillsammans med vår partner Globex Live kan ni livestreama alla matcher med AI-kameror som följer spelet automatiskt. Tittarna betalar per match eller för hela turneringen – en ny intäktskälla för cupen.
</CmFeatureRow>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-c3b90f52"
  eyebrow="ENGAGERA ERA BESÖKARE"
  title="Er egen mobilapp för Android och iPhone"
  ctaText="Skaffa en app för er turnering"
  ctaLink="/sv/app/"
  image="/media/home/usp-mobile-app.jpg"
  imageAlt="Egen mobilapp för turneringen"
  imagePosition="left"
  bgColor="white"
>
  Vi kan hjälpa er att få er egen mobilapp för turneringen. Vi gör allt arbete med att utveckla appen och den blir sedan kopplad till turneringen i Acme vilket gör att ni kan administrera allt från ett och samma ställe.
</CmFeatureRow>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-7f04b3a9"
  eyebrow="CASE STUDIE: FJORDBY BASKET FESTIVAL"
  title="En av våra kunder berättar"
  ctaText="Läs om Fjordby Basket Festival här"
  ctaLink="/sv/fjordby-basket-festival/"
  image="/media/home/customer-story.png"
  imageAlt="Fjordby Basket Festival"
  imagePosition="right"
  bgColor="light"
>
  Läs vårt reportage om en lyckad resa för basket och Fjordby i Norge. Ola Nordvik berättar lite om deras resa, hur de avancerat, lyckats och fortsätter att sätta upp nya mål i framtiden med sin turnering.
</CmFeatureRow>

<CmBandHeading id="band-5e17d8f0"
  heading="Mer information för den intresserade"
  bg="white"
  align="left"
  contained={true}
/>

<CmColumns id="cols-8b2f47c6"
  align="left"
  columns="2"
  gap="48"
  maxWidth={1140}
>
  <CmColumn id="col-d94a10e3"
    heading="Viktiga funktioner"
  >
    <TextBlock id="text-6c58e2b7">
      Missa inte att vi också har häftiga funktioner som livestreaming med Globex Live, liveresultat, egen hemsida för turneringen, boende & mat, domare, SMS-utskick och incheckning.
    </TextBlock>
    <CmButton id="btn-31f7a9d0"
      label="Läs mer om våra funktioner"
      href="/sv/missa-inte/"
      variant="green"
      icon="none"
    />
  </CmColumn>
  <CmColumn id="col-59a3e8d7"
    heading="Prissättning"
  >
    <TextBlock id="text-c21f80b4">
      Vi har en enkel prissättning som passar både små och stora turneringar i olika sporter. Förutom en lagbaserad licens finns det många extratjänster att välja till!
    </TextBlock>
    <CmButton id="btn-e40b97c3"
      label="Läs mer om våra priser"
      href="/sv/priser/"
      variant="green"
      icon="none"
    />
  </CmColumn>
</CmColumns>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-06c9e3b8"
  eyebrow="TA BETALT FÖR FÖRENINGEN"
  title="Acme Clubs"
  ctaText="Läs mer om Acme Clubs"
  ctaLink="https://clubs.acme.example/"
  image="/media/home/si.jpg"
  imageAlt="Acme Clubs"
  imagePosition="right"
  bgColor="light"
>
  Vår systerprodukt Acme Clubs används av uppemot 1000 klubbar för att samla in träningsavgifter och medlemsavgifter, i både Norge och Sverige. Systemet låter dig anpassa er insamling samtidigt som det är väldigt lättanvänt.
</CmFeatureRow>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-f15b72a0"
  eyebrow="IDROTT ÄR VIKTIGT I EN GLOBAL VÄRLD"
  title="Gemenskap, hopp och utveckling – både här hemma och i Östafrika."
  ctaText="Läs mer om samarbetet"
  ctaLink="/sv/lakeside-youth-cup/"
  image="/media/home/LakesideYouthCup.webp"
  imageAlt="Lakeside Youth Cup"
  imagePosition="left"
  bgColor="light"
>
  Vi samarbetar med Lakeside Youth Cup (LYC), en årlig ungdomsfestival i Tanzania som stärker unga genom idrott, utbildning och samhällsengagemang.
</CmFeatureRow>

</CmFeatureRow>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-7f04b3a9"
  eyebrow="CASE STUDY: FJORDBY BASKET FESTIVAL"

  ctaLink="/en/kort-och-klarna/"

    <CmButton id="btn-e40b97c3"

      icon="none"

  bgColor="light"

</CmFeatureRow>

<CmFeatureRow id="feat-f15b72a0"

  bgColor="light"

</CmFeatureRow>

prompt.system:
You are keeping the Swedish (sv) translation of a document up to date. Its source is English (en): Swedish was translated from it, and has since been corrected and localized by hand. The English page may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose Swedish pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in Swedish follow that convention too. Text a reader sees is Swedish, written as a Swedish writer would put it, not word for word.

Before you edit, write out briefly: every place where the Swedish page no longer says what the other pages say, quoted from both, with whether you think it is a change waiting to be made in Swedish or a difference on purpose, and why.

Then make the edits, together in one response. Edit with edit_file: its old_string must appear exactly, once, in the Swedish file. Each edit's result shows the Swedish file around it as it now reads. Look at it: if anything there is wrong, was missed, or now contradicts something elsewhere in the Swedish file, fix it with further edits. When the Swedish file is right, say in a sentence or two what you changed and why. If nothing needs to change, make no edit at all, and say why not. Write your plan, your notes and your summary in English, whatever language the documents are in.

The English page may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Text a reader sees is Swedish, written as a Swedish writer would put it, not word for word.

The English page may have changed since Swedish was last brought up to date. You have the current page of each other language and the current Swedish page. You have no diff and no earlier version, so you cannot see what changed: only how the pages compare as they are now.

Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:
- A fact that differs may need several edits in Swedish: everywhere Swedish states it, so that Swedish does not contradict itself.
- A difference may need no edit at all: when Swedish says the same thing in its own words, or leaves something out or adds something on purpose.
- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess. Call ask, once, with the question, the options you see, and what you would do if no one answered, and keep the content in question as it is unless you get an answer. Ask only when the answer changes what you write, never about wording or style.

Markup is not text. Component and attribute names, ids, front matter keys, file paths and URLs stay exactly as they are, except a link whose Swedish pages follow a convention of their own (a language prefix, a translated path): new links in Swedish follow that convention too. Your job is to bring the Swedish page up to date with the current English page: find what it says that Swedish does not, or says differently, and make the edits a careful editor of the Swedish page would make so that it says the same things.

The versions are not copies of each other. They may differ on purpose: wording, order, examples, local services and links, whole sections that only one language has. Many differences between the pages are deliberate, not changes waiting to be made. Keep all of that. It follows that:

- A difference in order or structure is not a reason to reorder Swedish.
- Something that only looks like a difference, but says the same thing, stays as it is.

Some things the documents cannot settle: two languages say different things about the same fact, or a change could mean two different things for Swedish. Then do not guess.
